basic_trek_information.overview: The Annapurna Base Camp Trek is a moderate journey through the Annapurna Conservation Area, taking trekkers to the base of the 10th highest mountain in the world. The trek passes through diverse landscapes from subtropical forests to high-altitude alpine terrain, traditional Gurung and Magar villages, and culminates at 4,130m in the Annapurna Sanctuary.
basic_trek_information.region: Annapurna Conservation Area, Gandaki Province (formerly Bagmati Province)

trek_duration.note: Depends on route (via Poon Hill is longer but better for acclimatization)

best_seasons.advantages: Clear skies, rhododendron blooms, moderate temperatures
Best visibility, stable weather, post-monsoon clear skies

best_seasons.challenges: Cold temperatures, possible snow at higher elevations

starting_point.name: Nayapul
starting_point.note: Traditional starting point; can also start from Hile or Jhinu Danda

ending_point.note: Most trekkers return to Nayapul and drive to Pokhara

day_by_day_itinerary_standard_11_day.route: Pokhara to Nayapul, trek to Hile
Ghorepani to Poon Hill (sunrise), then to Tadapani
day_by_day_itinerary_standard_11_day.note: Early morning sunrise hike to Poon Hill (30 min uphill)
Through rhododendron forest, along Modi Khola

day_by_day_itinerary_standard_11_day.route: Deurali to Machhapuchhre Base Camp to Annapurna Base Camp
Annapurna Base Camp to MBC to Deurali to Dovan/Bamboo
Ghorepani to Poon Hill (sunrise) to Nayapul to Pokhara
day_by_day_itinerary_standard_11_day.note: Final sunrise at Poon Hill, drive back to Pokhara

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What is the maximum altitude on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: 4,130 meters (13,550 feet) at Annapurna Base Camp

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: How many days does ABC Trek take?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: 7-12 days standard, 10-12 days via Poon Hill for better acclimatization

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What permits are required for ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: ACAP Permit (NPR 3,000) and TIMS Card (USD 20 individual)

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Is ABC Trek difficult?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Moderate to moderately difficult - requires reasonable fitness, 5-7 hours walking daily

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What is the total distance of ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: 75-85 km via Poon Hill, 50-70 km direct route

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I get altitude sickness on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes, moderate risk above 3,000m. Maximum 4,130m - gradual ascent and acclimatization days essential

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: When is the best time for ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Spring (March-May) and Autumn (September-November) - clear skies, stable weather

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Do I need a guide for ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Not mandatory but recommended. TIMS card requires either guide or trekking agency

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: How much does ABC Trek cost?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: $500-1,000 excluding international flights, depending on service level

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Are there tea houses on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes, 40-50 tea houses throughout the route with basic rooms and meals

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Is meat available on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Only below Chhomrong (2,170m). Above that, only vegetarian food due to no refrigeration

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I drink tap water on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: No - must boil, purify with tablets, or use UV sterilizer. Buy boiled water (USD 1-2/liter)

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Is Wi-Fi available on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes up to Deurali (fee NPR 300-500). Limited/unavailable above Deurali

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: How much does helicopter evacuation cost?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: $3,000-6,000 USD. Essential to have insurance covering high-altitude evacuation

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What should I pack for ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Warm layers, good boots, rain gear, water purification, first aid kit, pulse oximeter, headlamp

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Do I need trekking poles?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Recommended for steep descents, especially Poon Hill and Tadapani sections

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I charge my phone on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes, electricity available throughout (fee $2-3/device), mostly hydro/solar power

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Are hot showers available on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes below 2,500m (fee NPR 200-400, solar/gas heated). Limited above, mostly cold water

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What mountains can I see from ABC?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South (7,219m), Machhapuchhre (6,993m), Hiunchuli (6,441m), Gangapurna (7,455m)

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What mountains can I see from Poon Hill?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Full Annapurna range, Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Machhapuchhre, Nilgiri, Tukuche Peak - best sunrise viewpoint

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Is ABC Trek safer than Everest Base Camp?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes - max altitude 4,130m vs 5,364m, less extreme altitude sickness risk

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I do ABC Trek in winter?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes, but cold temperatures and possible snow above 3,500m. Less crowded, clear views

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: How do I get to Nayapul from Pokhara?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: 3-4 hour drive, 65km, mountainous road. Private jeep $40-60, shared $10-15

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What is the difference between MBC and ABC?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: MBC (3,700m) is Machhapuchhre Base Camp, last stop before ABC (4,130m). Both in Annapurna Sanctuary

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Are there monkeys on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes, langur monkeys in lower forest sections, especially near Ghorepani

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I see rhododendrons on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes, extensive rhododendron forests 2,000-3,500m, bloom spectacularly in spring (March-May)

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Is there a health post on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Basic health posts at Chhomrong and Jhinu Danda. No hospitals above. Serious cases need helicopter

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What emergency number for trekking in Nepal?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Police 100, Tourist Police 1144, Nepal Tourism Board +977-1-5356909

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I trek ABC without prior experience?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes, no technical sections needed. Good physical fitness essential, 5-7 hours daily walking

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What is the altitude of Ghorepani?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: 2,850 meters (9,350 feet)

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What is the altitude of Poon Hill?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: 3,210 meters (10,531 feet)

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Is ABC Trek suitable for beginners?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes, moderate difficulty with no technical climbing. Good fitness and preparation essential

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: How many liters of water should I drink daily?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: 3-4 liters to prevent dehydration and altitude sickness

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I bring my own tent for ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Not necessary - tea houses available everywhere. Camping only for special group arrangements

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What toilet facilities are on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Western-style below, squat toilets above. Shared facilities, sanitation generally decent

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Is Dal Bhat free on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Often unlimited/free for trekkers at many tea houses - traditional 'food for infinity'

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I see snow leopards on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Rare - snow leopards inhabit the area but sightings extremely uncommon. Himalayan thar more likely

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What is the best footwear for ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Sturdy waterproof trekking boots with good ankle support and grip

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Do I need sun protection on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Essential - high altitude UV exposure. Sunscreen SPF 50+, sunglasses, hat mandatory

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I use credit cards on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: No cash only. Carry NPR (Nepali Rupees) - no ATMs on trail

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What is the walking time daily on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Average 5-7 hours, 8-14 km per day depending on section

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Is ABC Trek crowded?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Moderately popular. Spring and autumn busiest. Winter less crowded

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I do ABC Trek solo?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes but guide recommended for safety, navigation, and TIMS card requirement

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What insurance do I need for ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Must cover high-altitude trekking to 4,200m+ and helicopter evacuation ($3,000-6,000)

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Is there mobile network on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes, NTC and Ncell coverage up to Deurali. Limited above, weather dependent

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What is the temperature at ABC in winter?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: -5°C to -15°C at night, can drop lower. Daytime 5-10°C

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I shower at ABC?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: No hot showers at ABC. Cold water only, not recommended due to extreme cold

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What is the lowest point on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Nayapul at 1,070 meters (3,510 feet)

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: How steep is the climb to Poon Hill?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: 3,767 stone steps, ~30 minutes uphill from Ghorepani. Steep but short

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can I see sunrise from ABC?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Yes, but Poon Hill is the better sunrise viewpoint. ABC offers sunset views

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Do I need a headlamp for ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Essential - early sunrise hikes, evening movement, no electricity after certain hours

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: What is the food cost on ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: $20-30/day average. Increases with altitude (2-3x at ABC vs Nayapel)

facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.question: Can babies/children do ABC Trek?
facts_frequently_asked_by_trekkers.answer: Not recommended below 10-12 years. Altitude 4,130m risky for young children
